subject: Biotechnology
title: Recombinant Growth Hormone
description: A quick, practical guide to Recombinant Growth Hormone.

hook.text: Growth hormone was once harvested from cadaver pituitary glands — some batches transmitted fatal brain disease.

buildup.text: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease from contaminated hormone killed over 200 children — the supply had to change.

discovery.text: Recombinant human growth hormone replaced cadaver sources in 1985 — E. coli produced unlimited, safe supply.

twist.text: Safe supply led to broader use — now prescribed for Turner syndrome, chronic kidney disease, and adult deficiency.

climax.text: The transition from cadaver to recombinant happened in just three years — biotech solved a deadly safety crisis.

punchline.text: From cadavers to bacteria — recombinant tech ended a tragedy.

quiz.question: Why was cadaver-derived growth hormone replaced?
options: It was too expensive to extract from pituitary glands
Some batches transmitted Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, a fatal brain disorder
It caused allergic reactions in all patients

details.summary: Recombinant human growth hormone replaced cadaver-derived growth hormone that caused fatal Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease in some recipients. Biosynthetic production ensured an unlimited safe supply for treating growth hormone deficiency in children and adults.
details.whyItMatters: The switch from cadaver-derived to recombinant growth hormone demonstrated biotechnology's capacity to replace dangerous biological extracts with safe synthetic alternatives. It saved lives and established a model for other recombinant hormones.
takeaways: Cadaver-derived growth hormone transmitted fatal prion disease to patients
Recombinant production eliminated transmission risk with unlimited supply
Growth hormone was approved in 1985 as one of the first recombinant drugs

faq.question: How did cadaver growth hormone cause Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease?
faq.answer: Growth hormone was extracted from thousands of pooled pituitary glands from cadavers. Prions causing CJD contaminated some batches and survived the purification process. Over 200 patients worldwide developed fatal CJD from contaminated growth hormone before recombinant production replaced it.

faq.question: What conditions does recombinant growth hormone treat?
faq.answer: Primary uses include growth hormone deficiency in children, Turner syndrome, chronic kidney disease in children, and adult growth hormone deficiency. Controversial off-label uses include anti-aging therapy and athletic performance enhancement, which lack evidence of benefit.
